_meta.what_this_is: A queue of fan-out tasks handed to a worker, in order. Each task has an outcome: 'ok' succeeds on the first try, 'flaky' fails a couple of times then succeeds, and 'poison' fails EVERY time (a malformed input, a permanently broken dependency). The worker retries failures. The question is what it does with a poison task. A correct worker retries up to max_retries, then moves the task to a dead-letter queue and continues; a broken worker retries forever and the poison task blocks every task behind it -- the whole fan-out stalls on one bad input.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. attempts_to_succeed is how many attempts a task needs (a huge number = poison); hand-authored so the drain, the dead-lettering, and the starvation are exact and checkable. attempt_budget bounds the simulation so a 'retry forever' bug is detectable rather than an infinite loop.
_meta.format: max_retries; attempt_budget (safety cap on total attempts); tasks [{id, kind, attempts_to_succeed}]
